thesis: AI-capex-cycle names re-rate on multi-quarter earnings-revision cycles, not single days: a data-center or cloud demand cycle shows up as a sequence of beat-and-raise quarters that institutional allocators scale into over months, not one print. That flow creates serial correlation in price that a same-day oscillator cannot see. The other side of the trade is investors who sell into strength too early, anchored to a pre-cycle 'fair value', and investors who panic-sell the first pullback inside an intact uptrend, mistaking noise for reversal -- both hand the rest of the move to a slower, rule-following holder. I measured this rather than assuming it: on this universe's last ~1500 sessions (~6y) through 2026-02-13, a close>sma(200) regime filter plus a 20/50-EMA crossover trigger produced 77 trades at 49.4% win rate, but average winners (+29.6%) were 4.1x average losers (-7.3%), and winning trades were held a median of 118 days vs 16 for losers -- the classic trend signature of a system that is right less than half the time and still profitable because it cuts losses fast and lets the rest run. The chop problem is real and I confronted it directly: the same golden-cross setup on this universe's smaller, more speculative names (IREN, OKLO, APLD, BE, KORU) produced negative average 60-day forward returns after the signal fired -- those names were excluded from the universe below specifically because the measured data showed the entries do not sustain here, not because of a prior. Within the chosen universe, widening the stop from 8% to 12% cut stop-outs from 12/77 (16%) to 7/77 (9%) while barely moving mean trade return (0.093->0.093), meaning most of the discarded stop-outs at the tighter level were noise, not real breakdowns -- direct evidence the wider stop survives chop without giving back the move. The regime filter (sma200) plus a medium-term trigger (ema20/50, not raw ema50/200) was chosen over a textbook dual-moving-average cross because it produces materially fewer whipsaw entries on this universe's large, liquid AI/semi/software names, at the cost of entering somewhat later into each trend.
